# Fiscal.ge

> Fiscal.ge is a Georgian and English guide to reviewed annual data on Georgia's state and municipal budgets, GDP, national economic sectors, regional economies, business, money and banks, unemployment, wages, poverty and inequality, education, science and culture, trade in goods and services, external flows, energy and food, the environment and climate, and population, and to Geostat's monthly consumer-price inflation.

**When to use Fiscal.ge:** Use it to understand, compare, and cite the published budget data, its scope, and its documented sources.

Budget and GDP data are annual, so it does not provide sub-annual or live budget reporting; inflation is the one monthly dataset, served through the MCP connection and the bulk files below. Fiscal.ge has a read-only MCP connection for AI clients at `https://fiscal.ge/mcp`, with production rate limits. The static bulk files below carry the same reviewed figures and remain available if the connection is temporarily paused. There is no REST query API, no write access, no accounts, and no datasets beyond those listed here. Each file carries its own sources, caveats and coverage — read them before citing a figure. Use the published figures only as documented, and do not invent values when data is unavailable or outside the stated scope.

## Core data

- [Fiscal.ge home](https://fiscal.ge/) — start with the site's scope and latest reviewed coverage.
- [Budget explorer](https://fiscal.ge/explorer) — choose a dataset and compare the published series.
- [National expenditure](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/expenditure) — annual state-budget expenditure.
- [National revenue](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/revenue) — annual consolidated-budget receipts.
- [Annual analysis](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/analysis) — one-year budget analysis.
- [Municipal budgets](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/municipalities) — annual municipal expenditure.
- [Government debt explorer](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/debt) — annual government debt stock, debt service and weighted-average interest rates.
- [Deficit explorer](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/deficit) — the IMF general-government balance as a share of GDP and in GEL, with IMF projection years marked.

- [Economy](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/economy) — the economy section: GDP, national economic sectors, GDP by expenditure and regional economies.
- [Economy overview](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/economy/gdp) — real GDP, annual real growth, nominal GDP and nominal GDP per person.
- [Economic sectors](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/economy/sectors) — 20 national economic activities plus a Total GDP reference.
- [GDP by expenditure](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/economy/expenditure) — what GDP is spent on: household and government consumption, investment, exports and imports, 2010–2025, as amounts, shares of GDP and real growth. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for it.
- [Regional economies](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/economy/regions) — choose one of 11 regions and explore total regional GDP plus 20 activities, 2010–2024.
- [Business](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/business) — the business section: Geostat's annual business statistics on firms' sales, jobs, investment, profit and loss, and firms opened and closed, 1999–2025. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for business.
- [Sales](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/business/sales) — firms' turnover in million GEL, 1999–2025, in total, by firm size (large, medium, small) and by Geostat's 14 industry groups.
- [Jobs](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/business/jobs) — persons employed in the firms Geostat surveys, 1999–2025, in total, by firm size and by industry; not the household survey's employment.
- [Investment and profit](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/business/investment-profit) — firms' investment in fixed assets, the profit of profit-making firms and the loss of loss-making firms, 2006–2025, each by firm size and industry; no net figure is calculated.
- [Firms opened and closed](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/business/firms) — active, new and closed firms by NACE section, 2014–2024, and Geostat's published birth and death rates.
- [Business by region](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/business/regions) — firms' sales and jobs by region on a map, with a page for Georgia and each of the 11 regions (regions from 2006; a firm's figures are counted in the region of its head office, so Tbilisi's figures can be overstated; the 11 regions do not add up to Georgia).
- [Housing and construction](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/housing) — the housing section: Geostat's annual building permits and completed buildings, 2006–2025, and its home price index and Tbilisi new-home asking prices, each year's fourth quarter. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for housing.
- [Building permits](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/housing/permits) — building permits issued in Georgia by number and floor area, in total and for 17 types of building, 2006–2025; a type Geostat published no column for in a year is a gap, not zero.
- [Completed buildings](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/housing/completed) — buildings completed and put into use by number and floor area, in total and by type of building, 2006–2025.
- [Home prices](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/housing/prices) — Geostat's residential property price index (2020 average = 100) for all homes, flats and houses, 2020–2025, and median asking prices per m² of newly built flats and houses in Tbilisi's ten districts, 2021–2025; each year is Geostat's fourth-quarter figure, and nothing is averaged.
- [Housing by region](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/housing/regions) — permitted floor area by region on a map, with a page for Georgia and each of the 11 regions showing permits and completed buildings, all buildings and residential, 2006–2025.
- [Inflation](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/inflation) — the inflation section.
- [Inflation overview](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/inflation/overview) — monthly national CPI inflation, core inflation, the price index and the National Bank of Georgia's target, as Geostat and the NBG publish them. The [inflation CSV](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-cpi-national.csv) carries every value; percentages are percentages (2.4 means 2.4%).
- [Inflation categories](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/inflation/categories) — the national CPI by its 12 COICOP divisions and 43 subgroups, the annual consumer-basket weights, and each group's contribution to annual inflation as derived by Fiscal.ge.
- [Inflation by city](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/inflation/cities) — annual inflation in Tbilisi, Kutaisi, Batumi, Gori, Telavi and Zugdidi from 2016 compared with Georgia's national rate, plus one page per city with its 12 COICOP divisions. Some prices (fuel, medicines, cars, mobile tariffs, flights) are recorded once and applied to every city.
- [Inflation by product](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/inflation/products) — reviewed current-basket products, published annual changes and Fiscal.ge-derived cumulative changes from monthly product indices. Discover current IDs, labels, coverage and identity limits in the catalogue; do not assume an old product name identifies today's product.
- [Money and banks](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/money) — the money-and-banks section: the National Bank of Georgia's annual money supply, bank loans and deposits, interest rates and bank-health measures, 1995–2025. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for money and banks.
- [Money supply](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/money/supply) — broad money (M3), broad money in lari (M2), narrow money (M1) and cash outside banks (M0) in million GEL from 1995, and all four as a share of GDP from 1996.
- [Loans and deposits](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/money/loans-deposits) — bank loans from 2002 and deposits from 1996, in total, in lari and in foreign currency; deposits of people from 2002 and of companies and organisations from 2015; and the share of loans and of deposits held in foreign currency.
- [Interest rates](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/money/interest-rates) — the National Bank of Georgia's policy rate from 2008 and the average rates on loans and on deposits from 1996, in total, in lari and in foreign currency.
- [Bank health](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/money/bank-health) — bad loans as a share of all loans from 2003, return on assets and on equity from 2001, and the two capital ratios from 2014.
- [Unemployment](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment) — the unemployment section: Geostat's annual Labour Force Survey estimates for Georgia, 2010–2025. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for unemployment.
- [Unemployment overview](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/overview) — unemployment, employment and participation rates and people counts for Georgia, with urban/rural, education and long-term tabs.
- [Unemployment by region](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/regions) — the latest unemployment rate of the 11 regions on a map and in a ranked list, with one page per region.
- [Unemployment by age](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/age) — the source-published age groups from 2020 onward.
- [Unemployment by gender](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/gender) — men and women beside the national rate.
- [Jobs by industry](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/industries) — the number of jobs by industry, 2017–2025, with the split for women and men from 2020.
- [Hours worked](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/hours) — usual weekly working hours, 2020–2025.
- [Informal jobs](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/informal) — the informal share of non-farm jobs, 2020–2025.
- [Young people not in work or study](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/unemployment/young-people) — the share of people aged 15–24 and 15–29 who are not in employment, education or training, 2020–2025.
- [Wages](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/wages) — the wages section: Geostat's annual average monthly nominal earnings and the Revenue Service median, gross lari per month, not adjusted for inflation. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for wages.
- [Wages overview](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/wages/overview) — Georgia's average monthly wage from 1995, for women and men from 1999 and public and non-public employers from 2000, and the median from 2018.
- [Wages by industry](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/wages/industries) — the 19 NACE Rev.2 sections from 2014 for each employer group, and the median by section from 2018.
- [Wages by region](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/wages/regions) — the average wage of the 11 regions from 2010 on a map, with one page per region.
- [Living standards](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/living-standards) — the living-standards section: household income and spending from 2002, poverty rates from 2004 and inequality from 2006, from Geostat's household surveys. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for living standards.
- [Household income](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/living-standards/income) — average monthly household income in Georgia by source, with towns, villages and regions compared, and one page per region.
- [Household spending](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/living-standards/spending) — average monthly household spending in Georgia by category, with towns, villages and regions compared, and one page per region.
- [Poverty](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/living-standards/poverty) — the share of people below the absolute poverty line (Georgia, towns, villages, age groups, women and men) and below 60% and 40% of median consumption, 2004–2025, and below the World Bank's international lines as republished by Geostat, 2004–2024.
- [Inequality](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/living-standards/inequality) — six Gini coefficients of income and expenditure, 2006–2025.
- [Health and social protection](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/health) — the health section: Geostat's annual healthcare statistics, 2002–2025, and registered deaths by cause for Georgia and its 11 regions, 2014–2025. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for health.
- [Doctors and hospitals](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/health/doctors-hospitals) — doctors by speciality and nursing staff, hospitals and out-patient clinics, hospital beds and out-patient visits for Georgia, 2002–2025; staff counting changed in 2012 and 2020, and four nursing groups stop in 2011.
- [Illnesses](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/health/illnesses) — new cases diagnosed each year by ICD-10 disease group, in thousands, and six single diseases (tuberculosis, HIV, diabetes, anaemia, syphilis and gonorrhoea), 2002–2025; diabetes and anaemia from 2016. Fiscal.ge adds no total of all new cases.
- [Causes of death](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/health/causes-of-death) — the crude death rate per 1,000 people of the 11 regions on a map, and one page each for Georgia and the regions with registered deaths by 20 groups of causes, COVID-19 included from 2020, 2014–2025.
- [Education](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/education) — the education section: Geostat's figures on schools (2000/01–2025/26), public kindergartens (2017/18–2025/26), universities (2010/11–2025/26) and vocational colleges (2013–2025). School years are labelled 2025/26 and stored by their start year. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for education.
- [Schools](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/education/schools) — pupils, teachers and general education schools on a municipality map, with a page for Georgia, each of the 11 regions and each of the 63 municipalities; regions and municipalities from 2005/06 (teachers from 2016/17), Georgia from 2000/01 with Geostat's public and private split, its pupils in thousands to one decimal.
- [Kindergartens](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/education/kindergartens) — children, staff and public kindergartens on a municipality map, with a page for Georgia, each region and each municipality, 2017/18–2025/26; public kindergartens only, and the staff count widens from 2020/21.
- [Universities](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/education/universities) — students and newly admitted students (2011/12–2025/26) and graduates (2010/11–2024/25, each calendar year's graduates under the school year they end), by level, public or private university, sex and eight fields of study.
- [Vocational colleges](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/education/vocational) — students admitted and graduates, 2013–2025, by sex and Geostat's nine current fields of study (most from 2019); the fields Geostat retired in 2019 are not shown, so the fields add up to less than the total up to 2020 for admissions and up to 2022 for graduates.
- [Science and culture](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/science-culture) — the science and culture section: Geostat's annual figures on researchers and research spending (2019–2024), patent applications and grants (2016–2025), museums and their visitors (2005–2025) and professional theatres (2006–2025). Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for science and culture.
- [Research](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/science-culture/research) — researchers by sex, degree, field and age, all research and development staff, the institutions doing research and their spending in million GEL, 2019–2024; Geostat collected the 2019 figures and the Ministry of Education, Science and Youth those from 2020.
- [Patents](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/science-culture/patents) — applications for inventions and utility models and the patents granted, from Georgian and foreign applicants by the national route and by the international route, 2016–2025, from Sakpatenti's data as Geostat publishes them.
- [Museums](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/science-culture/museums) — museum visitors by region on a map, with a page for Georgia and each of the 11 regions showing visitors and group tours (in thousands), exhibitions and museums, 2005–2025; Georgia's page adds the museum types and the staff (2020–2025).
- [Theatres](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/science-culture/theatres) — the audience of Georgia's professional theatres in thousands, their shows, the theatres by type and their seats, 2006–2025, events from 2021 and staff from 2020; the audience counts all events from 2021, performances only before, so 2020 and 2021 are not comparable.
- [Crime and justice](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/crime) — the crime and justice section: Geostat's annual criminal justice statistics, 2001–2025, each count also shown per 100,000 people, calculated by fiscal.ge from Georgia's population on 1 January. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for crime.
- [Recorded crimes](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/crime/recorded) — crimes recorded by every investigative agency, in total and by 11 types of crime, 2015–2025; counting changed in 2018, so 2017 and 2018 are not comparable.
- [Convictions](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/crime/convictions) — people convicted by the courts, by type of crime, age, sex and sentence, 2001–2025.
- [Prisons](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/crime/prisons) — prisoners at the end of each year by sex and age, 2001–2025, and sentenced or awaiting trial from 2010.
- [Victims](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/crime/victims) — victims of crime by sex, age and citizenship, 2007–2011 and 2015–2025; Geostat publishes nothing for 2012–2014.
- [Road accidents](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/crime/road-accidents) — road accidents, accidents caused by drunk driving, and the people killed and injured, 2001–2025; drunk-driving accidents cover the whole country only from 2025.
- [Trade](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/trade) — the trade section: Geostat's annual trade in goods and in services, in nominal USD. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for trade.
- [Trade overview](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/trade/overview) — total trade, exports, imports and the trade balance, 1995–2025.
- [Trading partners](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/trade/partners) — 212 countries and five published country groups (EU, CIS, BSEC, OECD, GUAM), 1995–2025, with end-year rankings; groups overlap and are never added up.
- [Products](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/trade/products) — exports and imports of 1,192 HS4 products, 2020–2025.
- [Domestic exports](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/trade/domestic-exports) — total exports, domestic exports and re-exports, 2014–2025, by country and for 99 products plus Other commodities.
- [Services trade](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/trade/services) — services exports, imports, turnover and balance, in total and for 12 service types, 2020–2024.
- [Trade composition](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/trade/composition) — goods exports and imports by ten SITC goods groups or seven published BEC economic categories, 2000–2025; the two views are alternative classifications of the same trade.
- [External flows](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/external) — the external-flows section: money transfers, foreign direct investment, the current account, foreign debt and international reserves, in nominal USD. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for external flows.
- [Money from abroad](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/external/money-from-abroad) — the National Bank of Georgia's money transfers received and sent, in total and by country, 2000–2025; partial years are marked.
- [Foreign investment](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/external/foreign-investment) — Geostat's foreign direct investment inflow by country (1996–2025), sector (2016–2025) and region (2009–2025).
- [Current account](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/external/current-account) — the National Bank of Georgia's BPM6 current account and its four parts, 2000–2025, in USD or as a share of GDP.
- [Foreign debt](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/external/foreign-debt) — the National Bank of Georgia's gross external debt of the whole country by who owes it (government, banks, companies, loans between related companies, National Bank), 2006–2026, in USD or as a share of GDP; the 2026 point is the end of June.
- [Reserves](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/external/reserves) — the National Bank of Georgia's international reserves in foreign currency, gold and SDRs, 1995–2026, in USD or as a share of GDP; the 2026 point is the end of September.
- [Energy and food](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/energy-food) — the energy-and-food section: Geostat's annual energy balance, 2013–2024, food self-sufficiency ratios, 2014–2025, and farming (farm output, harvests, livestock and farm-gate prices), 2006–2025. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for energy and food.
- [Energy supply](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/energy-food/energy-supply) — domestic energy supply by fuel, production, imports and exports, in thousand tonnes of oil equivalent.
- [Electricity](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/energy-food/electricity) — electricity production by plant type, imports, exports, final consumption by user and network losses, in GWh.
- [Energy use](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/energy-food/energy-use) — final energy consumption by user and by fuel, in thousand tonnes of oil equivalent.
- [Food self-sufficiency](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/energy-food/food-self-sufficiency) — the self-sufficiency ratio, in percent, of twelve foods: wheat, maize, potatoes, vegetables, grapes, meat (with beef, pork, sheep and goat meat, and poultry), milk and eggs.
- [Farming](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/energy-food/farming) — farm output in million ₾, 2010–2025 (2025 preliminary), harvests of thirteen crops, livestock numbers, and meat, milk and eggs, 2006–2025, and twelve farm-gate prices in ₾, 2014–2025, from Geostat's agriculture statistics.
- [Environment and climate](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment) — the environment section: Geostat's annual greenhouse gas and air pollutant emissions, city air quality, temperature and rainfall, water, municipal waste and forests. Values are shown as Geostat's tables print them. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for the environment.
- [Greenhouse gases](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment/greenhouse-gases) — Georgia's greenhouse gas emissions, 2000–2022, in million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent: the total, the total after forests and land absorb, by sector, energy in detail and by gas, and emissions per person.
- [Air pollution](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment/air-pollution) — emissions of eight air pollutants (carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, ammonia, volatile organic compounds, all dust, PM10 and PM2.5), 2013–2024, in thousand tonnes, from factories, power plants and homes and from vehicles.
- [City air quality](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment/air-quality) — yearly averages at 16 monitoring stations in nine cities, 2005–2025, with a page per city: fine dust PM10 and PM2.5 and nitrogen dioxide against the yearly limits, and the days over the daily PM10 limit; Zestaponi's manual station measures dust, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and manganese dioxide.
- [Temperature and rain](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment/climate) — yearly average temperature, its difference from the 1961–1990 average, and yearly rain and snow for Georgia, Tbilisi and the warmest, coldest, wettest and driest regions; Geostat prints 1990, 1995 and every year from 2000 to 2024.
- [Water](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment/water) — water put into the pipes, lost on the way and reaching users, 2015–2025, in million m³; the share lost; people with piped water, sewers and wastewater treatment; household use per person.
- [Waste](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment/waste) — municipal waste taken to landfills, 2015–2024, in thousand tonnes, on a region map, with a page for Georgia and each of the 11 regions; Georgia's waste per person.
- [Forests](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/environment/forests) — timber cut and illegal logging found, 2010–2024, in m³, on a region map, with a page for Georgia and each of the 11 regions; Georgia's protected areas, forest and field fires and area burnt. Tbilisi has no timber figure.
- [Demography](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/demography) — the demography section: Population, Age and sex, Migration, and Births, deaths and fertility.
- [Population](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/demography/population) — population on 1 January for Georgia (2004–2026), its 11 regions and 64 municipalities (2015–2026) with a clickable map, and density for Georgia and the regions. Figures from 2025 are based on the 2024 census and are not comparable with earlier years, so no growth or change is computed. Browse-only for now: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for demography.
- [Migration](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/demography/migration) — immigrants and emigrants for Georgia, 2012–2025, by sex and six citizenship groups (Georgia, Russia, Turkey, Azerbaijan, Ukraine, and other countries, added up by Fiscal.ge), with net migration. Border-crossing records: citizenship is not country of birth or residence. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for demography.
- [Births, deaths and fertility](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/demography/births-deaths) — registered live births and deaths for Georgia (2014–2025), its 11 regions and 64 municipalities (2015–2025), with births per 100 deaths; Georgia's total fertility rate, fertility by mother's age and life expectancy at birth. Each Population place page also carries that place's births and deaths. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for demography.
- [Age and sex](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/demography/age-sex) — Georgia's population pyramid on 1 January of every year, 2004–2026, with an optional comparison year; each five-year age group's share by year; and, as a glance at the foot of the page, the 11 regions by share aged 65 and over in the 2024 census (counted on 14 November 2024). Figures from 2025 are based on the 2024 census, so no difference is computed across that re-base. Georgia's and each region's Population page also carries its census pyramid. Browse-only: there is no MCP tool and no bulk file for demography.

## Methodology and sources

- [Methodology hub](https://fiscal.ge/methodology) — how the reviewed public data is prepared and presented.
- [Expenditure methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/expenditure) — national-expenditure sources and processing.
- [Revenue methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/revenue) — national-revenue sources and processing.
- [Municipal methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/municipalities) — municipal-expenditure sources and processing.
- [Government debt methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/debt) — debt stock, principal and interest payments, the portfolio's average interest rates and original sources.

- [GDP methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/gdp) — price bases, series coverage, preliminary status and original sources.
- [Economic sectors methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/economic-sectors) — sector GVA versus GDP, GDP shares, annual real growth and preliminary status.
- [GDP by expenditure methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/gdp-expenditure) — the expenditure identity, imports shown as positive amounts, GDP shares, real growth and preliminary status.
- [Regional economies methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/regional-economies) — regional GVA at basic prices, regional GDP at market prices, calculations and original sources.
- [Business methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/business) — Geostat's survey of enterprises and business demography: turnover, persons employed, investment, profit and loss, firm sizes, the 2006 coverage change, regions and original files.
- [Housing methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/housing) — Geostat's building permits and completed buildings, the home price index (fourth quarter of each year), Tbilisi asking prices, definitions, gaps and original files.
- [Inflation methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/inflation) — Geostat CPI definitions, validation, the NBG target and original files.
- [Money and banks methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/money) — National Bank of Georgia money, loan, deposit, interest-rate and bank-health definitions and original files.
- [Unemployment methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/unemployment) — Labour Force Survey definitions, age-band and regional changes, and original files.
- [Wages methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/wages) — average and median earnings, gross nominal lari, NACE Rev.2 sections and original files.
- [Household income and spending methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/household-income) — Geostat's household survey, per-household and per-person averages, income sources, spending categories and original files.
- [Poverty methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/poverty) — absolute, relative and international poverty lines, the Gini coefficients and original files.
- [Health methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/health) — Geostat's healthcare and causes-of-death tables, the 2012 and 2020 staff counting changes, new cases, ICD-10 chapters, the death rate and original files.
- [Education methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/education) — Geostat's school, kindergarten, university and vocational tables: school years and graduates, Georgia's pupils in thousands, the 2020/21 kindergarten staff and 2015/16 master's changes, the old vocational fields, Geostat's own sums and original files.
- [Science and culture methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/science-culture) — Geostat's research, patent, museum and theatre tables: the 2020 change of collector for the research figures, Sakpatenti's national and international routes, museum visitors by region, the 2021 theatre audience change, events from 2021 and original files.
- [Crime and justice methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/crime) — Geostat's criminal justice tables and the agencies behind them, what a recorded crime is, the 2018 counting change, sentence types, prisoners on 31 December, the rates per 100,000 people and original files.
- [Trade methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/trade) — FOB exports, CIF imports, partner and product identities, re-exports and original files.
- [External flows methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/external-flows) — money transfers, BPM6 balance of payments, Geostat FDI and original files.
- [Energy and food methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/energy-food) — Geostat's energy balance and food balance sheets, units and original files.
- [Environment and climate methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/environment) — Geostat's environment tables: values as the tables print them, gaps, the climate years, city yearly limits, the manual Zestaponi station, regions and original files.
- [Demography methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/demography) — Geostat population and density, the 1 January 2025 census re-base, definitions and original files.

## Bulk data files

- [GDP overview](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/gdp-overview.json) — six series with explicit units, bilingual definitions, missing years, statuses and sources. The [GDP CSV](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/gdp-overview.csv) retains reviewed decimal values. Use `query_gdp` for selected series and years; growth values are percentages (7.5 means 7.5%), not fractions. Nominal GDP per person is not average income.
- [Economic sectors JSON](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/economic-sectors.json) and [economic sectors CSV](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/economic-sectors.csv) — use `query_economic_sectors` for national activity/reference selection, annual years and one measure: `amount_gel`, `share_of_gdp_pct` or `real_growth_pct`. Nominal GEL and GDP shares cover 2010–2025; real growth covers 2011–2025, with 2010 explicitly missing. Sector amounts are GVA at basic prices; Total GDP uses market prices. Shares use all national GDP and need not sum to 100%. Percent values use 7.5 for 7.5%; growth rates are not contributions and must not be summed. 2025 is preliminary. Sector rankings and cumulative comparisons are unsupported.
- [Regional economies JSON](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/regional-economies.json) and [regional economies CSV](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/regional-economies.csv) — 6,930 reviewed cells for 11 regions, Total regional GDP and 20 activities, 2010–2024. Use `query_regional_economies` for selected regions, activities, years and either `amount_gel` or `share_of_region_gdp_pct`. Activities are GVA at basic prices; the share denominator is the same region's complete market-price GDP. It does not serve 2025, real growth, per-capita values or a region's share of Georgia's GDP.
- [Inflation, national](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-national.json) — monthly national CPI in every published measure, the National Bank of Georgia target and annual basket weights; each observation carries its `period` (YYYY-MM), unit, sources and caveats. Use `query_inflation`; 2.4 means 2.4%.
- [Inflation categories CSV](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-categories.csv) and [its metadata](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-categories.json) — COICOP group price changes and Fiscal.ge-derived contributions in percentage points, with a residual that closes each month on the published headline. Contributions are an approximation, not Geostat figures.
- [Inflation cities CSV](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-cities.csv) and [its metadata](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-cities.json) — annual and monthly rates for the six Geostat price-collection cities from 2016, total and 12 COICOP divisions, plus the total's 12-month average. Use `query_inflation` with `entityIds`; 2.4 means 2.4%.
- [Inflation products CSV](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-products.csv) and [its metadata](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/inflation-products.json) — exact published base-100 annual/monthly inputs, with missing indices blank and explicitly unavailable. These CSV indices are not percentage changes. `query_inflation_products` accepts `yoy_pct` (published annual index minus 100) or `cumulative_pct` with `startYear`: Fiscal.ge compounds every monthly index from January of that year through the endpoint, relative to the previous December. Never sum rates, fill missing inputs or bridge reviewed product splits. Cumulative observations and rankings identify `calculationBasePeriod`. Annual `compare` reports percentage-point rate differences, not price growth between endpoints; cumulative comparison is unsupported. `rank` considers the entire current roster with explicit exclusions, default 10 / maximum 100 entries. Retired products, city products, retail GEL prices, product weights/contributions and a price calculator are outside scope.
- [Data manifest](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/manifest.json) — every published file with its row count, byte size and SHA-256.
- [Government debt](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/government-debt.json) — debt stock and debt service in GEL, with the interest rates in a file of their own.
- [General government balance](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/general-government-balance.json) — the IMF's deficit or surplus measure; values are signed.
- [Capability catalogue](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/catalogue.json) — the datasets, entities, series and exclusions that exist.
- [Source resolution](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/sources.json) — every logical source with its public originals or its stated derivation.

The manifest lists every dataset file, so they are reachable without repeating them here. Budget figures are published in GEL with the GDP and population denominators alongside; shares and per-resident values are reproducible from those, not precomputed. Two files are the exception, because their figures have no GEL form: debt interest rates are percent per annum, and the general government balance is a share of GDP whose published GEL amount travels beside it. Balance values are signed - a negative value is a deficit.

## AI connection

- [Connect an AI assistant](https://fiscal.ge/connect) — connection address, setup and coverage.
- [Connect an AI assistant in English](https://fiscal.ge/en/connect) — the same endpoint, with English instructions and examples.

Data schema 1.6.0 adds internal_error and the preserved_derived source-narrowing outcome. It retains current-product inflation, the optional cumulative calculationBasePeriod, monthly period (YYYY-MM) and reviewed Georgian (*Ka) and English (*En) labels, definitions, missing-value explanations, comparison reasons, ranking descriptions and source evidence. Generic fields retain original wording and mandatory attributions. documentLanguage is null unless verified; an English title does not imply an English source document. Catalogue search accepts either language. Translation corrections change dataVersion. Existing requests remain compatible, with no language argument; clients must accept additive fields and data schema 1.6.0 rather than require byte-identical output. Strict clients caching output enums must refresh discovery and update exact-version validation. Human pages use /en for English; /mcp, /downloads/data/, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and /llms.txt remain shared.

Paired example questions:
- „რამდენი დაიხარჯა სახელმწიფო ბიუჯეტიდან განათლებაზე 2025 წელს?“ / “How much did the state budget spend on education in 2025?”
- „როგორ შეიცვალა ხულოს მუნიციპალური ხარჯები 2024 წლიდან 2025 წლამდე და შედარებადია თუ არა ჯამები?“ / “How did Khulo’s municipal expenditure change from 2024 to 2025, and are the totals comparable?”
- „რა იყო დამამუშავებელი მრეწველობის წილი იმერეთის რეგიონულ მშპ-ში 2024 წელს?“ / “What was manufacturing's share of Imereti's regional GDP in 2024?”
- „რამდენი იყო სახელმწიფო ვალის პორტფელის შეწონილი საშუალო საპროცენტო განაკვეთი 2024 წელს?“ / “What was the government debt portfolio’s weighted-average interest rate in 2024?”
- „სახელმწიფო მმართველობის სექტორის ბალანსის რომელი წლებია პროგნოზი და რას ნიშნავს უარყოფითი მნიშვნელობა?“ / “Which general government balance years are forecasts, and what does a negative value mean?”
- „რამდენი იყო საქართველოს წლიური ინფლაცია ბოლო გამოქვეყნებულ თვეში?“ / “What was Georgia's annual inflation in the latest published month?”
- „ფასების შემგროვებელი ქალაქებიდან რომელში იყო სურსათის წლიური ინფლაცია ყველაზე მაღალი ბოლო გამოქვეყნებულ თვეში?“ / “Which measured city had the highest annual food inflation in the latest published month?”
- „რამდენი პროცენტული პუნქტით შეიცვალა ბათუმის წლიური ინფლაცია ორ გამოქვეყნებულ თვეს შორის?“ / “How did Batumi's annual inflation rate change between two published months, in percentage points?”
- „მოქმედი კალათის რომელ პროდუქტებს ჰქონდა ფასის ყველაზე მაღალი წლიური ზრდა ბოლო გამოქვეყნებულ თვეში?“ / “Which current-basket products had the highest annual price increases in the latest published month?”
- „რამდენით შეიცვალა შერჩეული პროდუქტის ფასი კუმულაციურად მითითებული პირველი წლის იანვრიდან ბოლო თვემდე, წინა დეკემბერთან შედარებით?“ / “How much did a selected product's price change cumulatively from January of a stated first year through an endpoint, relative to the previous December?”

The endpoint is `https://fiscal.ge/mcp`, stateless unauthenticated MCP over Streamable HTTP. Modern protocol 2026-07-28 uses server/discover and per-request metadata; legacy 2025-11-25 uses initialization. Protocol revisions are separate from data schema 1.6.0. Both return finite JSON without sessions or subscriptions; GET and DELETE are unsupported. If it returns 429, respect Retry-After; if temporarily unavailable, use https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/manifest.json. Its current read-only tools are describe_coverage, query_national, query_ministries, query_municipal, query_debt, query_deficit, query_gdp, query_economic_sectors, query_regional_economies, query_inflation, query_inflation_products, compare, rank, get_sources; tools/list is authoritative. Call describe_coverage first with one meaningful keyword — it returns actual ids, measures and year/month ranges, so nothing has to be guessed. If a phrase returns no matches, try its principal word or browse the named dataset; a failed phrase match is not proof that data is absent. Keep expectedDataVersion consistent across calls. A coverage span does not guarantee complete history. Every answer carries its sources and any caveats that qualify it; preserve units, missing values and projections, and cite the returned original documents and Fiscal.ge. Annual-rate comparisons are percentage points; a cumulative product answer is derived by Fiscal.ge, and its monthly source originals are upstream inputs. For products, discover first and request only the required series and dates. Requests retain the 500-cell and 512 KiB complete-result limits; narrow an oversized request or use the published bulk files rather than discard evidence.
